blocks.text: Read the chapter with this setting in view: A second sign act portrays a foolish or worthless shepherd who neglects the vulnerable flock and receives a judgment woe. It gives a starting point for following the chapter's own movement. The chapter itself should determine how far the point is taken. A more precise reconstruction remains disputed.

A literary feature to notice is that Zechariah 11 commands a shepherding sign act over a doomed or exploited flock and names two staffs Favor and Union, which the shepherd breaks. This form helps organize the chapter's claims. Notice it before drawing broader conclusions from a single phrase or image. Interpretations differ on some details.
